questions.q:
Match each situation in Column I with its expression in Column II. n is a number of rupees or metres as stated.
Column I: 1. A ribbon of n metres from which 4 metres are cut off  2. The cost in rupees of 4 pencils priced n rupees each  3. Two notes of n rupees each, after 9 rupees are spent  4. Nine notes of n rupees each, after 2 rupees are spent
Column II: A. 2n - 9  B. n - 4  C. 9n - 2  D. 4n
In a calendar month, a block of dates 2 rows by 3 columns is chosen. The bottom middle date is w. Write an expression, in w, for each of the other five dates (a week has 7 days).
questions.a: Bottom row: w - 1, w, w + 1. Top row, one week earlier: w - 8, w - 7, w - 6.
s: Bottom left w - 1 and bottom right w + 1
Top left w - 8 and top right w - 6

questions.q: A village sports club fences a rectangular kabaddi ground that is l metres long and b metres wide on all four sides, but leaves a gate of g metres unfenced. Fencing wire is sold only in rolls of 50 m, and the club can pay for 3 rolls. The ground now measures 42 m by 30 m with one gate of 4 m. (a) Write an expression for the length of wire needed. (b) Find the length for the present ground. (c) Write the expression if there are two gates of g metres each, and find the length. (d) The club wants to lengthen the ground to 48 m. Can 3 rolls do it with one gate, or with two gates? Recommend a plan.
questions.a: (a) 2l + 2b - g. (b) 2 × 42 + 2 × 30 - 4 = 140 m. (c) 2l + 2b - 2g; 84 + 60 - 8 = 136 m. (d) Lengthened to 48 m: with one gate 96 + 60 - 4 = 152 m, more than the 150 m in 3 rolls; with two gates 96 + 60 - 8 = 148 m, which 3 rolls cover. So lengthen the ground and make two gates.
s: Part (d): 152 m does not fit, 148 m fits, so recommends two gates

questions.q: A trader packs k biscuits in each of 6 boxes, sells 2 of the boxes with all their biscuits, and then gives 9 biscuits from the remaining boxes away as samples. Which expression gives the biscuits left?
In s = a + 3, Shabnam's age s is 3 years more than Aftab's age a. Aftab is 4 years old today and will be 10 six years later. By how much does Shabnam's age change over the same six years, and why?
questions.a: By 6 years, because the fixed gap of 3 years in the relation does not change
o: By 6 years, because the fixed gap of 3 years in the relation does not change
By 9 years, because the gap of 3 years is added on top of the 6 years that pass
By 3 years, because only the 3 in the relation is able to change with time
By 13 years, because Shabnam is 13 years old when Aftab is 10 years old

questions.q: A photo studio charges ₹80 for the sitting and ₹25 for each printed photo, and takes ₹30 off the total bill for students. Which expression gives a student's bill in rupees for p photos?
Ketaki buys c coconuts at ₹35 each and j kg of jaggery at ₹60 per kg. Rohan says her bill is (35 + 60) × (c + j). Test his expression with 2 coconuts and 1 kg of jaggery, and say whether he is right.
questions.a: No. For c = 2, j = 1 the real bill is 35 × 2 + 60 × 1 = ₹130, but Rohan's expression gives 95 × 3 = ₹285. The correct expression is 35c + 60j.
s: Finds the true bill ₹130 for c = 2, j = 1
Finds that Rohan's expression gives ₹285, so he is wrong

questions.q: A shop earns 40m + 15n rupees when it sells m shirts at ₹40 each and n caps at ₹15 each. The owner then lowers the price of every shirt by ₹5 and leaves the price of a cap unchanged. (a) Write the new expression for the money earned. (b) Write, in terms of m only, how much less the shop earns for the same sales, and find this for 12 shirts.
questions.a: (a) 35m + 15n. (b) The shop earns 5m rupees less, because each of the m shirts brings ₹5 less and the caps are unchanged; for 12 shirts this is 5 × 12 = ₹60 (check: 40 × 12 - 35 × 12 = 60).
s: Part (a): 35m + 15n, with only the shirt price changed
Part (b): 5m less, which is ₹60 for 12 shirts

questions.q: Using t for the number, write '11 less than 3 times t' and '3 less than 11 times t'. Are the two expressions the same? Give a reason.
questions.a: 3t - 11 and 11t - 3. They are not the same: for t = 2 the first is -5 and the second is 19 (the operations are applied in a different order).
s: Says they differ, with a reason or a test value

questions.q: Nandini jogs 4 km every day in the first week. In each later week she increases her daily distance by q km over the previous week. (a) How far does she jog in week 1? (b) Write the daily distance and the weekly distance in week 2. (c) Write the weekly distance for week 3. (d) Write an expression for the distance in all three weeks together (no need to simplify). (e) Find the total if q = 1.
s: Part (b): 4 + q a day and 7(4 + q) in the week
Part (c): 4 + 2q a day and 7(4 + 2q) in the week
Part (d): adds the three weekly distances in an expression
Part (e): substitutes q = 1 and gets 105 km

questions.q: Dev is d years old and his cousin Kavya is 4 years younger. In 5 years' time the sum of their ages in years will be 2d + ___.

Rekha has ₹x. She spends ₹40 on a book, and her mother then doubles the money Rekha has left. Rekha writes the final amount as 2x - 40. (a) Write the correct expression. (b) For x = 100, find the correct amount and the amount Rekha's expression gives, and say what her expression has done wrongly.
questions.a: (a) 2(x - 40), because the doubling applies to what is left after the book is bought. (b) The correct amount is 2 × 60 = ₹120; Rekha's expression gives 200 - 40 = ₹160, which is ₹40 too much. Her expression doubles all the money first and only then takes away the 40, so the ₹40 spent is also doubled.
s: Part (a): 2(x - 40) with the bracket for the money left
Part (b): ₹120 against ₹160, and says the 40 is taken off after the doubling instead of before

questions.q:
Assertion (A): A cab charges ₹15 on booking plus ₹9 for each km, so the fare for k km is 15 + 9k rupees. For a trip of 2k km the fare is 15 + 18k, not 2 × (15 + 9k).
Reason (R): The booking charge is paid once, so doubling the distance doubles only the part that depends on k.
questions.a: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

questions.q: A school canteen sells tea at ₹12 a cup and samosas at ₹8 each. (a) Write an expression for the money in rupees from t cups of tea and s samosas. (b) The canteen also pays ₹150 for gas each day. Write an expression for what is left after paying for the gas. (c) On Monday it sold 10 cups of tea and 5 samosas; on Tuesday 8 cups and 4 samosas. Use your expression from (b) to find what is left on each day, and say what the sign of each answer tells the canteen.
questions.a: (a) 12t + 8s. (b) 12t + 8s - 150. (c) Monday: 120 + 40 - 150 = ₹10 left, a profit of ₹10. Tuesday: 96 + 32 - 150 = -₹22, a loss of ₹22 (the sales did not cover the gas).
s: Part (c): reads the positive value as profit and the negative one as loss

questions.q: True or False: A pen costs ₹20. Ishaan buys n pens and then 3 more pens, and says the total cost is 20n + 3 rupees. Test with n = 2 and give the reason or correction.
questions.a: False. For n = 2 he buys 5 pens costing ₹100, but 20n + 3 = 43. The 3 extra pens cost 3 × 20 = ₹60, not ₹3, so the total is 20n + 60, that is 20(n + 3).
s: States the verdict False, supported by the test values 100 and 43
Corrects it to 20n + 60 or 20(n + 3), because each extra pen costs ₹20

questions.q: A farmer keeps h hens and g goats in a shed. (a) Write an expression for the total number of legs. (b) He sells 3 hens and 2 goats. Write an expression for the legs left, and find its value for h = 10 and g = 6.
questions.a: (a) 2h + 4g. (b) 2(h - 3) + 4(g - 2); for h = 10, g = 6 this is 2 × 7 + 4 × 4 = 30 legs (check: 44 legs at first, 14 legs sold).

questions.q:
A tailor charges ₹60 for stitching plus ₹35 for every metre of cloth, so the cost for m metres is 60 + 35m rupees. Consider the statements.
Statement 1: A customer who paid ₹235 bought 6 metres of cloth.
Statement 2: For 2k metres the cost is 60 + 70k rupees.
Statement 3: For (m + 1) metres the cost is 95 + 35m rupees.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: 2 and 3 only

questions.q: A school charges a lab fee of ₹150 once plus ₹40 for every lab session, so a student who takes n sessions should pay 150 + 40n rupees. A clerk by mistake billed every student 190n rupees. (a) Find what the clerk's bill and the correct fee are for a student with 1 session and for a student with 4 sessions. (b) Explain why the mistake did not show up when the clerk checked the bill of a student with 1 session. (c) Find the overcharge for students who took 2, 3 and 5 sessions. (d) The school will refund only students overcharged by more than ₹250. Which of these three students get a refund?
questions.a: (a) 1 session: 190 and 190; 4 sessions: 760 and 310. (b) For n = 1 both give 190, so the check hid the mistake; for other values they differ. (c) 2 sessions: 380 - 230 = 150; 3 sessions: 570 - 270 = 300; 5 sessions: 950 - 350 = 600. (d) The students with 3 and 5 sessions (300 and 600 are more than 250); the one with 2 sessions (150) does not.
s: Part (a): 190 and 190 for 1 session; 760 and 310 for 4 sessions
Part (b): the two expressions agree only at n = 1, so one test value cannot reveal the mistake
Part (d): refunds for 3 and 5 sessions only, with the comparison to 250

questions.q: Create a real-life situation (a story with what each letter stands for) that is described by the expression 30n + 100.
questions.a: A caterer charges ₹100 as a fixed delivery fee and ₹30 for each plate. For n plates the bill is 30n + 100 rupees. (Any consistent situation is accepted.)
s: Explains 30n as 30 for each of n things
Explains 100 as a fixed amount added once

questions.q: At a school fete, x stalls sell tea only, y stalls sell snacks only and z stalls sell both. Every stall that sells tea puts up one red flag and every stall that sells snacks puts up one green flag. How many flags are needed in all?
questions.a: x + y + 2z

questions.q: Anu works out 4p - 3q for p = -2 and q = -3 and gets -17. Which slip explains her answer?
o: She ignored the minus sign of q and used q = 3, so she worked out -8 - 9
She ignored the minus sign of p and used p = 2, so she worked out 8 + 9
She swapped the two values and worked out 4 × (-3) - 3 × (-2)
She worked out (4p - 3) × q instead of 4 times p, less 3 times q
questions.a: She ignored the minus sign of q and used q = 3, so she worked out -8 - 9

questions.q: True or False: Because the numbers and signs are the same, 3 + 4m and (3 + 4)m take the same value for every m. Test with m = 2 and give the reason or correction.
questions.a: False. For m = 2, 3 + 4m = 3 + 8 = 11 but (3 + 4)m = 7 × 2 = 14. In 3 + 4m only the 4 is multiplied by m; the bracket makes the whole 7 multiply m.
s: States the verdict False, with the test values 11 and 14
Explains that the bracket changes which number m multiplies

questions.q: A fruit seller's profit in rupees is 15x - 200 when she sells x kg. On a day she sells only 10 kg, what does the expression show?
questions.a: A loss of ₹50

questions.q: In an inter-school quiz, a team's score is 5c - qw, where c is the number of correct answers, w the number of wrong answers, and q the marks lost for each wrong answer. The quiz master is yet to choose q. Team A answered 12 correctly and 9 wrongly; Team B answered 10 correctly and 3 wrongly; Team D answered 3 correctly and 12 wrongly. (a) With q = 2, find the scores of Team A and Team B. (b) With q = 2, find Team D's score and say what a negative score means here. (c) Find the scores of Team A and Team B if q = 0 and if q = 4. (d) The quiz master wants to discourage wild guessing but not to wipe out teams that answer a few wrongly. Which value of q from 0, 2 and 4 would you suggest? Use your numbers.
questions.a: (a) A: 60 - 18 = 42; B: 50 - 6 = 44. (b) D: 15 - 24 = -9; the marks lost for wrong answers exceed the marks earned. (c) q = 0: A 60, B 50. q = 4: A 24, B 38. (d) q = 0 rewards guessing (A, with 9 wrong, wins); q = 4 cuts Team A to 24 and punishes a few errors heavily; q = 2 puts the careful team B ahead by 2 marks yet keeps A close. A reasoned choice of 2 is expected; any value justified from the figures is accepted.
s: Part (b): -9 with the meaning that penalties exceed marks earned
Part (c): 60 and 50 for q = 0, 24 and 38 for q = 4
Part (d): recommends a value of q and justifies it with the scores

questions.q: The temperature in a cold store, in degrees Celsius, is 6 - 3h at h hours after the cooling machine is switched on. (a) Find the temperature at h = 0, 2 and 4. (b) Find the first whole number of hours after which the temperature is below -5 degrees.
questions.a: (a) h = 0: 6; h = 2: 6 - 6 = 0; h = 4: 6 - 12 = -6. (b) At h = 3 the value is -3, which is not below -5; at h = 4 it is -6, which is. So the first whole hour is 4.
s: Part (b): 4 hours, since h = 3 gives -3 and h = 4 gives -6

questions.q: Write an expression in x with two terms whose value is 5 when x = 0 and 17 when x = 3. Show the check for both values.
questions.a: 4x + 5. For x = 0 it gives 5, and for x = 3 it gives 4 × 3 + 5 = 17.

questions.q: A worksheet shows four calculations by students. Check each one. (i) If c = -2, then 6 - c = 4. (ii) If n = 2, then 3n + 4 = 18. (iii) If m = -5, then 2(m + 3) = -4. (iv) If p = 4 and q = 3, then p - (5 - q) = -4. For each wrong one, say what went wrong and give the correct value; for a correct one, say so.
questions.a: (i) Wrong: 6 - (-2) = 6 + 2 = 8 (the minus sign of c was ignored). (ii) Wrong: 3 × 2 + 4 = 10; the student added 4 to n first and then multiplied by 3, which is 3(n + 4). (iii) Correct: 2 × (-2) = -4. (iv) Wrong: 4 - (5 - 3) = 4 - 2 = 2 (the minus before the bracket was not applied to q).
s: Part (i): corrects to 8 and names the ignored negative
Part (ii): corrects to 10 and names the wrong order of operations
Part (iii): says it is correct, checking -4
Part (iv): explains the minus outside the bracket changes the sign of q

questions.q: In the sports week of a school, a house scores in three events: 6g - 2f, 5g - 3f and 9g - f, where g is the points for a gold medal and f the points deducted for a foul. Take g = 5 and f = 2. (a) Find the score in event 1. (b) Find the score in event 2. (c) Find the score in event 3. (d) Find the total. (e) The trophy needs a total of at least 90 points. Does g = 5 earn it? If not, find the smallest whole number g (keeping f = 2) that does.
questions.a: (a) 6 × 5 - 2 × 2 = 26. (b) 5 × 5 - 3 × 2 = 19. (c) 9 × 5 - 2 = 43. (d) 26 + 19 + 43 = 88. (e) 88 is less than 90, so g = 5 does not earn the trophy. For g = 6 the events give 32, 24 and 52, total 108, which is at least 90; so the smallest whole g is 6.
s: Part (e): says 88 is short of 90 and finds g = 6 with total 108

questions.q: A school plants 4 saplings in each of n pits and then moves 3 saplings to another site. Rani writes the number of saplings left as 4n - 3 and, for n = 6, calculates 4 × 3 = 12. What is the correct value?
Kunal says that when h = 9, the expression 2h has the value 29. What did he do wrong? Give the correct value.
questions.a: He wrote the 2 and the 9 side by side as 29. 2h means 2 × h, so the value is 2 × 9 = 18.
s: Identifies the digits were joined as 29 instead of multiplied

questions.q: An auto-rickshaw bill in rupees is 50 + 12k for a ride of k km. Ravi takes a 5 km ride and Meena takes an 8 km ride, each paying a separate bill. How much do the two pay together?
When m = -2, the expression 5 - 3m + 2m takes the value ___.
(a) Find the value of 3a - 2b for a = 5 and b = 4. (b) Find it again after the two values are swapped (a = 4, b = 5). Does swapping the values give the same result?
questions.a: (a) 3 × 5 - 2 × 4 = 7. (b) 3 × 4 - 2 × 5 = 2. No: the two results differ, since a and b have different multipliers.
s: Part (b): 12 - 10 = 2 and says swapping changes the value

questions.q:
A data pack gives 900 MB, and the data left after n days of use is taken as 900 - 150n MB (a negative value means data bought beyond the pack). Consider the statements.
Statement 1: After 6 days the value is 0.
Statement 2: From day 3 to day 5 the value falls by 150.
Statement 3: On day 2 the value is 600.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: 1 and 3 only

questions.q: In a trekking game a team earns 3 points for each flag f it collects and loses 2 points for each penalty p, so its score is 3f - 2p. Team X collects 6 flags and gets 4 penalties; Team Y collects 5 flags and gets 1 penalty. Which team leads and by how much?
questions.a: Team Y leads by 3 points

questions.q: In a kabaddi league a team's points after a season are 8x + 3y, where x is the points for each win and y the points for each draw. (a) Find the total when x = 4 and y = 2. (b) Find the total if draws earn nothing (y = 0), and say how many points the draws were worth in part (a).
questions.a: (a) 8 × 4 + 3 × 2 = 38. (b) 8 × 4 + 0 = 32; the draws were worth 38 - 32 = 6 points.

questions.q: A cab firm charges ₹25 plus ₹14 for every km, that is 25 + 14k rupees. Find the fare for 6 km and for 12 km, and then show how much more the 12 km ride costs than the 6 km ride.
questions.a: 6 km: 25 + 14 × 6 = ₹109. 12 km: 25 + 14 × 12 = ₹193. The difference is ₹84, which is 14 × 6: the fixed ₹25 is paid in both rides and cancels.
s: Difference ₹84 with the reason that ₹25 is common

questions.q: Hari says that 7 - y has a bigger value when y = -2 than when y = 2. Test his claim and say whether it is right.
questions.a: Yes, he is right. For y = -2, 7 - (-2) = 9; for y = 2, 7 - 2 = 5; and 9 is bigger than 5. Subtracting a negative number adds, so a negative y makes 7 - y larger.
s: Finds 5 for y = 2 and says Hari is right
Explains that subtracting a negative adds

questions.q: A tea stall owner's daily profit in rupees is 18x - 240, where x is the number of litres of tea she sells (a negative value is a loss). (a) Find the profit or loss for 10, 14 and 20 litres. (b) Find the values for 13 and 14 litres and say by how much one more litre changes the profit. (c) What is the smallest whole number of litres that gives a profit? (d) She expects to sell anything from 12 to 16 litres a day; she could instead take a job that pays a sure ₹30 a day. Find her profit at 12 and at 16 litres and advise her, with reasons.
questions.a: (a) 10 litres: -60 (a loss of 60); 14 litres: 12; 20 litres: 120. (b) 13 litres: -6; 14 litres: 12; one more litre adds 18. (c) 14 litres (13 gives a loss of 6). (d) At 12 litres she loses 24 and at 16 litres she gains 48. At 15 litres the profit is exactly 30, so the stall beats the sure 30 only if she sells at least 16 litres (14 litres gives only 12). Since she may sell as few as 12 litres and lose 24, the sure job is safer unless she is confident of more than 15 litres. Any advice that uses these figures is accepted.
s: Part (b): -6 and 12, and one more litre adds 18
Part (d): -24 and 48, and advice justified from the figures against the sure 30

questions.q:
Assertion (A): For b = -3, the expression 8 - b has the value 5.
Reason (R): Subtracting a negative number is the same as adding the corresponding positive number.
questions.a: A is false but R is true.
o: A is false but R is true.
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.

questions.q: A school hall must seat exactly 96 students. Four-seater benches cost ₹1,800 each and take 2 square metres of floor each. Six-seater benches cost ₹2,600 each and take 3.5 square metres each. The hall has 58 square metres free and the budget is ₹45,000. Any free floor left over can be hired out for events at ₹300 per square metre for the year. (a) Write expressions, for n four-seater benches, for the seats, the cost and the floor area; then the same three for n six-seater benches. (b) How many benches of each kind seat exactly 96? (c) Find the cost and floor area of each choice and check that both fit. (d) For each choice find the cost minus the first-year hire income from the floor left over, and say which choice the school should make.
questions.a: (a) Four-seater: 4n seats, ₹1800n, 2n sq m. Six-seater: 6n seats, ₹2600n, 3.5n sq m. (b) 24 four-seater benches and 16 six-seater benches. (c) Four-seaters: ₹43,200 and 48 sq m. Six-seaters: ₹41,600 and 56 sq m. Both fit within 58 sq m and ₹45,000. (d) Four-seaters leave 10 sq m: 43,200 - 3,000 = ₹40,200. Six-seaters leave 2 sq m: 41,600 - 600 = ₹41,000. The four-seater choice is cheaper by ₹800 after the first year, even though the six-seaters cost ₹1,600 less to buy.
s: Part (c): ₹43,200 with 48 sq m and ₹41,600 with 56 sq m, both fitting
Part (d): net ₹40,200 and ₹41,000, so the four-seater choice by ₹800

questions.q:
Consider the statements about the values of expressions in short form.
Statement 1: For p = 3 and q = 4, the expression 6p - 2q has the value 4.
Statement 2: For n = 5, the expression 3n + 4 has the value 19.
Statement 3: The expression 5 × (x + 2) can be written in short form as 5x + 2.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: 2 only

questions.q: (a) Write 'seven times the sum of a and b' and 'seven times a, plus b' in short form. (b) Find both values for a = 2 and b = 3 and say which part of the first expression the second one leaves out.
questions.a: (a) 7(a + b) and 7a + b. (b) 7 × 5 = 35 and 14 + 3 = 17; the second multiplies only a by 7, so b is not multiplied.
s: Part (b): values 35 and 17 with the reason that b is not multiplied by 7 in the second

questions.q: The multiples of 7 are 7, 14, 21, 28, ... (a) Write the 15th term and the nth term. (b) Aryan says 150 is a term of this sequence. Is he right? Give a reason.
questions.a: (a) 15th term 7 × 15 = 105; nth term 7n. (b) No. The terms near 150 are 7 × 21 = 147 and 7 × 22 = 154, so 150 falls between two terms.
s: Part (b): says no, citing 147 and 154 as the neighbouring terms

questions.q: A print shop charges a fixed binding fee plus a rate per page. Anita printed 5 pages and her bill was ₹40. Which charging rule, with p the number of pages, gives exactly this bill?

A hall has rows of 15 chairs each. (a) Write an expression for the chairs in n rows and find it for 24 rows. (b) The manager can either remove one whole row from the 24 rows or remove one chair from every row. Find the chairs left in each case. (c) Which leaves fewer chairs, and by how many?
questions.a: (a) 15n; 15 × 24 = 360. (b) One row removed: 15 × 23 = 345. One chair from every row: 14 × 24 = 336. (c) Removing one chair from every row leaves fewer, by 9 chairs.

questions.q: Zoya says that 5m + 3 and 5(m + 3) are the same expression. Test her claim with m = 2 and say whether she is right.
questions.a: No. For m = 2, 5m + 3 = 5 × 2 + 3 = 13, but 5(m + 3) = 5 × 5 = 25. In 5m + 3 only m is multiplied by 5; in 5(m + 3) the whole of m + 3 is.
s: Explains what is multiplied by 5 in each

questions.q: A teacher gives the expressions 4n, 9 + n, 2n + 6 and 6n - 5 and says that three of them take the same value when n = 3. Which expression is the odd one out?
Show that no term of the sequence 4, 8, 12, 16, ... (nth term 4n) can be an odd number.
questions.a: 4n = 2 × (2n), and 2n is a whole number whenever n is, so every term is 2 times a whole number. Such a number is even, so an odd number cannot be a term.
s: Notes that 2n is a whole number
Concludes every term is even, so none is odd

questions.q: The multiples of 6 are 6, 12, 18, 24, ... with nth term 6n. Which statement about these terms is correct?
o: The 14th term equals the sum of the 5th term and the 9th term
The 10th term is half of the 5th term in the sequence
The 14th term equals the 5th term plus the number 9 itself
The 14th term equals the 5th term times the 9th term
questions.a: The 14th term equals the sum of the 5th term and the 9th term

questions.q: Two sequences are 12, 24, 36, 48, ... and 11, 22, 33, 44, ... (a) Write the nth term of each. (b) Which is larger, the 29th term of the first or the 31st term of the second, and by how much?
questions.a: (a) 12n and 11n. (b) 12 × 29 = 348 and 11 × 31 = 341, so the 29th term of the first sequence is larger by 7.

questions.q: Neha saves ₹50 in month 1, ₹100 in month 2, ₹150 in month 3 and so on in the same pattern. Her cousin Rahul saves ₹400 every month. (a) Write Neha's deposit in month n. (b) Find Neha's deposit in month 18. (c) Who deposits more in month 18, and by how much? (d) Neha says, 'I deposit more than Rahul every month.' Test her claim in months 4, 8 and 9. (e) Find the first month in which Neha deposits more than Rahul.
questions.a: (a) 50n. (b) 50 × 18 = ₹900. (c) Neha, by 900 - 400 = ₹500. (d) Month 4: 200 against 400; month 8: 400 against 400 (equal); month 9: 450 against 400. So her claim is wrong for months 1 to 8. (e) Month 9.
s: Part (d): 200 vs 400, 400 vs 400, 450 vs 400, so the claim is wrong

questions.q: (a) A square of side q cm has perimeter 4q cm. Its side is increased by 3 cm. Write the new perimeter and find it for q = 12. (b) By how much has the perimeter grown, and does this depend on q? Explain.
questions.a: (a) 4(q + 3); for q = 12 it is 4 × 15 = 60 cm. (b) It grows from 48 to 60, by 12 cm. This is 4 × 3 and does not depend on q: each of the four sides grows by 3.
s: Part (b): growth 12 cm, equal to 4 × 3 for every q

questions.q:
Match each expression in Column I with its value for x = 3 in Column II.
Column I: 1. 5x + 3  2. 5(x + 3)  3. 3x + 5x  4. 5x - 3x
Column II: A. 6  B. 18  C. 24  D. 30

A farmer's income in rupees is 25a + 40b for a quintals of wheat and b quintals of rice. The price of rice rises by ₹10 per quintal and the price of wheat is unchanged. Which expression gives the new income?
The expression 6p + 4 has the value 40 when p = 6. When p is increased from 6 to 9, the value of the expression increases by ___.

Parthiv makes matchstick L shapes (2 sticks each) and T shapes (3 sticks each) for a display. He has 280 matchsticks and will use all of them. The art teacher says the display must have at least 50 T shapes; within that, the class wants as many shapes as possible. (a) Write an expression for the sticks needed for n L's and m T's. (b) Plan A is 50 L's and 60 T's; Plan B is 80 L's and 40 T's. Show that both use exactly 280 sticks and find the number of shapes in each. (c) Plan C is 65 L's and 50 T's. Check that it uses 280 sticks and count its shapes. (d) Which of A, B and C meets the teacher's rule and makes the most shapes? Explain why trying 51 or more T's cannot beat C.
questions.a: (a) 2n + 3m. (b) Plan A: 100 + 180 = 280 sticks, 110 shapes. Plan B: 160 + 120 = 280 sticks, 120 shapes. (c) Plan C: 130 + 150 = 280 sticks, 115 shapes. (d) B breaks the rule (only 40 T's). Of A and C, C makes the most shapes (115 against 110). Each extra T uses 3 sticks, while the 3 sticks of an L pair make 1.5 L's, so each T gives up more shapes than it adds; with 50 T's already required, 50 is the best number of T's and C cannot be beaten.
s: Part (d): C is best among those meeting the rule, with the reason that more T's cost more sticks per shape

questions.q: The expression 5x - 2 takes the values 3, 8 and 13 for x = 1, 2 and 3. (a) Without substituting 4, say what value it takes at x = 4 and why. (b) Find the value at x = 10, and say what the coefficient 5 tells you about how the value changes when x grows by 1.
questions.a: (a) 18, because the value goes up by 5 every time x goes up by 1, and 13 + 5 = 18. (b) 5 × 10 - 2 = 48. The coefficient 5 is the amount the value increases by for each increase of 1 in x.
s: Part (a): 18, with the reason that each step of 1 in x adds 5
Part (b): 48, and the coefficient 5 is the change per unit step in x

questions.q: A shop sells n pencils at ₹7 each, charges ₹12 for packing the order, and takes ₹20 off the total with a coupon. What is the bill for n = 6?

Four students worked on short forms and values. (i) 8 × p + 3 for p = 4: 'the short form is 8p + 3 and the value is 35'. (ii) q × 6 - 2 × r for q = 5, r = 3: 'the short form is 6q - 2r and the value is 24'. (iii) 5 × (m + 2) for m = 3: 'the short form is 5m + 2 and the value is 17'. (iv) Raju says 6a + 1 for a = 3 has the value 6 × (3 + 1) = 24. Check each and correct any mistake.
questions.a: (i) Correct: 8 × 4 + 3 = 35. (ii) Correct: 6 × 5 - 2 × 3 = 24. (iii) Wrong: the bracket is lost; the short form is 5(m + 2) and the value is 5 × 5 = 25. (iv) Wrong: only a is multiplied by 6, so the value is 6 × 3 + 1 = 19; Raju added 1 to a first.
s: Parts (i) and (ii): confirms both, with 35 and 24
Part (iii): spots that the bracket is lost and writes 5(m + 2)
Part (iv): identifies that 1 was added to a before multiplying

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The cost in rupees of n books at ₹45 each and one bag at ₹350 is 45n + 350.
Reason (R): The bag costs more than seven of these books together.
questions.a: Both are true (7 × 45 = 315 < 350), but R does not explain A.
o: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

questions.q: Imran says that 5a + 4b - 2a + 3b simplifies to 3a + b. Test his answer by putting a = 1 and b = 1 in the original expression and in his answer, and say whether he is right.
questions.a: Partly right. For a = 1, b = 1 the original is 5 + 4 - 2 + 3 = 10 but his answer gives 3 + 1 = 4, so he is wrong. His a-terms are right (5a - 2a = 3a) but the b-terms are 4b + 3b = 7b, not b. The correct form is 3a + 7b, which gives 10.
s: Finds 10 for the original and 4 for his answer, so it is not correct
Says the 3a part is right and the b part is wrong

questions.q: A florist sells garlands at ₹g each and loose-flower packets at ₹f each. On Monday she sold 7 garlands and 9 packets; on Tuesday 12 garlands and 4 packets; 6 packets from the two days were returned and refunded. (a) Write the money she kept, in simplest form. (b) Find it when g = 45 and f = 10.
s: Part (a): 19g + 7f, with the 6 returned packets removed from the 13 sold

questions.q: A shop sells pens at ₹c each. It sells 6 pens on day one, 4 more than that on day two, and twice the day-two number on day three. When c = 8, the shop earns ₹___ in all.

Match each expression in Column I with its simplest form in Column II.
Column I: 1. 6a + 2b - 3a - 5b  2. 6a - 2b + 3a + 5b  3. 6a - (2b + 3a) + 5b  4. 6a - (2b - 3a) - 5b
Column II: A. 3a - 3b  B. 9a + 3b  C. 3a + 3b  D. 9a - 7b
Write an expression with four terms that simplifies to 5x + 3y. Show how it simplifies.
questions.a: For example 9x + 2y - 4x + y. Combine x terms: 9x - 4x = 5x; combine y terms: 2y + y = 3y; result 5x + 3y. (Any correct example is accepted.)
s: Gives an expression with four terms of x and y
Combines the like x terms correctly
Combines the like y terms and reaches 5x + 3y

questions.q: A stationer sells notebooks at ₹n and pens at ₹p. Over three days she sold 6, 2 and 9 notebooks and 3, 8 and 5 pens. Which is her total sale in simplest form?
(a) Simplify 5a + 8b - 3 + 6a - 2b - 9a + 10. (b) How many terms does the simplest form have, and why can they not be combined further?
questions.a: (a) a terms: 5 + 6 - 9 = 2, b terms: 8 - 2 = 6, numbers: -3 + 10 = 7, so 2a + 6b + 7. (b) Three terms; they are unlike (a, b and a plain number), so none can be added to another.
s: Part (b): three terms, unlike so cannot combine

questions.q: (a) Add 5m - 3n + 6 and 2n - 9 + 4m. (b) Subtract 3a + 2b - 5 from 7a - b + 4. (c) Check your answer to (b) with a = 2 and b = 1.
s: Part (b): 4a - 3b + 9 with every sign inside the second bracket reversed

questions.q: True or False: The expression 6m - 2n + 4m + 2n can be written as 10m. Test with m = 3 and n = 5 and give the reason or correction.
questions.a: True. For m = 3 and n = 5 the original is 18 - 10 + 12 + 10 = 30 and 10m = 30. The terms -2n and +2n are like terms whose numbers -2 and +2 add up to 0, so no n is left, and 6m + 4m = 10m.
s: States True, supported by the test values 30 and 30
Reasons that -2n and +2n are like terms that cancel, leaving 6m + 4m = 10m

questions.q: A rectangular vegetable plot is 4x metres long and 3x metres wide. A farmer fences all four sides. Which expression, in simplest form, gives the length of fencing in metres?

A camp store takes a deposit of 50x + 200y rupees for x sleeping bags and y tents, and refunds 15x + 60y rupees when they are returned, so the store keeps the difference. The assistant writes the amount kept as 50x + 200y - 15x + 60y = 35x + 260y. (a) Test the assistant's result with x = 2 and y = 1 by working out the deposit, the refund and the amount kept directly. (b) Write the correct simplest form and check it with the same values. (c) Group A takes 12 bags and 4 tents; Group B takes 4 bags and 6 tents. How much too much would the assistant's formula charge each group? (d) Show that the excess depends only on y and not on x, and find the total the store would have to give back to A and B.
questions.a: (a) Deposit 100 + 200 = 300, refund 30 + 60 = 90, kept 210; the assistant's formula gives 70 + 260 = 330, so it is wrong. (b) The refund is subtracted as a whole: 50x - 15x = 35x and 200y - 60y = 140y, so 35x + 140y; for x = 2, y = 1 it gives 70 + 140 = 210, which matches. (c) Correct amounts: A 420 + 560 = ₹980, B 140 + 840 = ₹980. The assistant's formula gives A 420 + 1,040 = ₹1,460 and B 140 + 1,560 = ₹1,700, so the excess is ₹480 and ₹720. (d) The two simplest forms have the same 35x and differ only in 260y against 140y, so the excess is 120y, whatever x is. The total to give back is 480 + 720 = ₹1,200 (120 × 10).
s: Part (a): 300, 90 and 210 against 330, so the assistant is wrong
Part (c): excess ₹480 for A and ₹720 for B
Part (d): excess is 120y, independent of x, total ₹1,200

questions.q: (a) In 12m - 5n + 7m + 3, which terms are like terms? (b) Combine them and write the expression in its simplest form.
questions.a: (a) 12m and 7m, which involve the same letter-number m (-5n involves n, and 3 is a plain number). (b) 12m + 7m = 19m, so the simplest form is 19m - 5n + 3.
s: Part (a): picks 12m and 7m as the like terms

questions.q: For the annual day, a ribbon roll costs ₹a and a balloon pack costs ₹b. Committee P buys 12 rolls and 5 packs for the stage and 7 rolls and 9 packs for the gate. Committee Q buys 15 rolls and 8 packs in all. (a) Write P's total in simplest form. (b) Write, in simplest form, how much more P spends than Q. (c) Find the amounts for P and Q when a = 40 and b = 25. (d) Next year every roll and every pack costs ₹5 more. By how much does P's bill rise, by how much does Q's rise, and why do they not rise equally?
questions.a: (a) 19a + 14b. (b) (19a + 14b) - (15a + 8b) = 4a + 6b. (c) P: 760 + 350 = ₹1,110; Q: 600 + 200 = ₹800. (d) P buys 19 + 14 = 33 items, so its bill rises by 33 × 5 = ₹165; Q buys 15 + 8 = 23 items, so its bill rises by 23 × 5 = ₹115. P's bill rises ₹50 more, because P buys 10 more items and each costs ₹5 more.
s: Part (d): rises of ₹165 and ₹115, with the reason of 33 items against 23

questions.q: Chitra buys 9 packets of biscuits at ₹b a packet and 5 packets of juice at ₹2b a packet for a school picnic, and then returns 4 biscuit packets and 1 juice packet. How much has she spent, in simplest form?

A fruit seller earns ₹p on each kg sold and loses ₹q on each kg that spoils. Her three days gave 6p - 2q, 5p - 4q and 8p - q, and her neighbour's three days gave 21p - 5q in all. (a) Find the seller's total. (b) Find how much more the neighbour made, in simplest form. (c) Who made more, if p and q are positive?
questions.a: (a) (6 + 5 + 8)p - (2 + 4 + 1)q = 19p - 7q. (b) 21p - 5q - (19p - 7q) = 2p + 2q. (c) The neighbour, since 2p + 2q is positive.
s: Part (b): 2p + 2q after removing the bracket with its minus sign
Part (c): the neighbour, because the difference is positive

questions.q: A rectangular board is n units wide and 15 units long. A poster covers a strip 6 units long across the whole width of the board. (a) Write the area of the whole board and the area the poster covers. (b) Find the uncovered area by subtracting, in simplest form. (c) A second poster covers a strip 4 units long, also across the whole width, in the uncovered part. Write the area still uncovered in simplest form. (d) Find the length of the strip still uncovered and use it to write the area again. (e) Check the answers of (c) and (d) for n = 4.
questions.a: (a) 15n and 6n. (b) 15n - 6n = 9n. (c) 15n - 6n - 4n = 5n. (d) The strip left is 15 - 6 - 4 = 5 units long, so its area is 5n. (e) 60 - 24 - 16 = 20 and 5 × 4 = 20.

questions.q:
Consider the following about simplifying.
Statement 1: 9x - 4y + 2x + 4y - 5 simplifies to 11x - 5.
Statement 2: When x = 3, the expression 9x - 4y + 2x + 4y - 5 has the same value for y = 1 and for y = 10.
Statement 3: Adding 5a - 2b and 3b - 5a gives b.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: 1, 2 and 3

questions.q: The four sides of a quadrilateral flower bed are (2a + 3) m, (a + 5) m, (3a - 1) m and (a + 2) m. (a) Write the perimeter in simplest form. (b) For a = 3, find each side and confirm that the perimeter you wrote matches their sum.
questions.a: (a) 2a + a + 3a + a = 7a and 3 + 5 - 1 + 2 = 9, so 7a + 9. (b) For a = 3 the sides are 9, 8, 8 and 5 metres, which add up to 30 m, and 7 × 3 + 9 = 30.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The expression 7x - 3y + 2x - 5y simplifies to 9x - 8y.
Reason (R): Both 7x - 3y + 2x - 5y and 9x - 8y have the value 1 when x = 1 and y = 1.
questions.a: Both are true (7 - 3 + 2 - 5 = 1 and 9 - 8 = 1), but one matching test value does not explain why the simplification is right.
o: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

questions.q: Ria simplifies 2d - d - (d - c) as 2d - d - d - c and writes -c. Checking with d = 3 and c = 5 gives a different value. What is the correct simplest form?
questions.a: c

questions.q: A bike shop takes an advance of (30a + 55b) rupees for a and b of two kinds of spare part and returns (8a + 15b) rupees on cancelling. Which expression gives the amount it keeps?
Create a situation about money that is described by (25m + 60n) - (5m + 12n). Say what m and n stand for and what each bracket means.
questions.a: A shop takes a deposit of ₹25 for each of m chairs and ₹60 for each of n tables, and gives back ₹5 per chair and ₹12 per table on return. The first bracket is the deposit paid, the second the refund, and the difference is the money the shop keeps. (Any consistent story is accepted.)
s: Says what m and n stand for
Explains the first bracket as an amount paid
Explains the second bracket as an amount taken off or returned

questions.q: The expression 5(2w + 3) - 4w simplifies to 6w + ___.

A sweet shop sells a box of 4 laddus (₹l each) and 2 barfis (₹b each). A caterer orders 8 boxes. Offer 1 gives one laddu free in every box. Offer 2 gives a flat ₹50 off the whole bill. Take l = 6 and b = 15. (a) Write the bill for 8 boxes with no offer, in simplest form. (b) Write the bill under Offer 1 in simplest form. (c) Find the bills with no offer, with Offer 1 and with Offer 2. (d) Which offer is better for 8 boxes? A party of 12 boxes also asks: which is better for them, and why does the answer change?
questions.a: (a) 8(4l + 2b) = 32l + 16b. (b) 32l + 16b - 8l = 24l + 16b. (c) No offer ₹432; Offer 1 ₹384; Offer 2 ₹382. (d) 8 boxes: Offer 2 is better by ₹2. 12 boxes: no offer ₹648, Offer 1 ₹576, Offer 2 ₹598, so Offer 1 is better by ₹22. Offer 1 saves ₹6 per box, so it grows with the number of boxes while Offer 2 stays ₹50.
s: Part (d): Offer 2 for 8 boxes, Offer 1 for 12 with the reason

questions.q: A student's work is shown. Check each line and correct the wrong ones. (i) 3 + (a + 6) = 3a + 18. (ii) 8p - p + 6q - 2q = 7p + 4q. (iii) 9 - (4 - 5z) = 5 - 5z. (iv) 7 - 2(m - 3) = 5m - 15. (v) 4(2r + 3) = 8r + 3.
questions.a: (i) Wrong: a + 9 (the bracket has a plus, nothing is multiplied). (ii) Correct. (iii) Wrong: 9 - 4 + 5z = 5 + 5z. (iv) Wrong: the student subtracted 2 from 7 before multiplying; 7 - 2m + 6 = 13 - 2m. (v) Wrong: 4 × 2r + 4 × 3 = 8r + 12.
s: Line (iv): corrects to 13 - 2m and names the wrong order
Line (v): corrects to 8r + 12 using the distributive property

questions.q:
Assertion (A): 4(x + y) - y simplifies to 4x + 3y.
Reason (R): A multiple of a sum equals the sum of the multiples, so 4(x + y) = 4x + 4y, and 4y - y = 3y.
questions.a: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

questions.q: Tara says: 'Both 9 - (2 + y) and 9 - (2 - y) are equal to 7 - y.' Test each part with y = 3 and y = 10, and say whether she is right.
questions.a: Partly right. 9 - (2 + y) = 7 - y is true: y = 3 gives 4 and 4, y = 10 gives -3 and -3. 9 - (2 - y) = 7 - y is false: y = 3 gives 9 - (-1) = 10 but 7 - 3 = 4. The minus before the bracket changes both signs, so 9 - (2 - y) = 9 - 2 + y = 7 + y.
s: Confirms the first part with y = 3 (4 and 4) and y = 10 (-3 and -3)
Shows the second part fails: y = 3 gives 10 against 4
Corrects it to 7 + y by changing both signs in the bracket

questions.q: (a) Open the brackets in 3(2a + 5b - 4) - 2(a - b) + 12 and simplify. (b) Check your answer with a = 1 and b = 1.
s: Part (a): 4a + 17b, with the sign of b changed in the second bracket

questions.q: Show that the value of 3(x + 4) - 3x is the same whatever number x stands for, and check it for x = 0 and x = 10.
questions.a: 3(x + 4) - 3x = 3x + 12 - 3x = 12, with no x left. Check: x = 0 gives 3 × 4 - 0 = 12; x = 10 gives 3 × 14 - 30 = 12.
s: Checks x = 0 and x = 10 both give 12

questions.q: (a) Simplify 15x - (6x - 2y). (b) Check your answer by evaluating both the original and your result for x = 2 and y = 3.
questions.a: (a) 15x - 6x + 2y = 9x + 2y. (b) Original: 30 - (12 - 6) = 24; result: 18 + 6 = 24. They agree.
s: Part (a): 9x + 2y with the sign of 2y changed

questions.q: Simplify 3(4r + 2s + 7) - 21 - 12r - 6s. What do you notice about the answer?
questions.a: 3(4r + 2s + 7) = 12r + 6s + 21, so the expression is 12r + 6s + 21 - 21 - 12r - 6s = 0. Every term cancels and the value is 0 whatever r and s are.
s: Cancels to 0 and says it holds for every r and s

questions.q:
Consider the following about brackets.
Statement 1: (9a + 7b) - (4a + 2b) simplifies to 5a + 5b.
Statement 2: m - (n - 4) can be written as m - n + 4.
Statement 3: A minus sign before a bracket changes the sign of only the first term inside it.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: 1 and 2 only

questions.q: A tank holds (x + 3) litres. Two litres are poured in and then (x - 1) litres are drawn out. What is the simplest form of the litres now in the tank?
A trader buys 4 crates, each holding (3m + 2) mangoes, and sells (5m + 1) of the mangoes. Which expression, in simplest form, gives the mangoes left?

A hostel orders 5 kits, each with one bedsheet costing ₹s and one pillow cover costing ₹c. Two covers arrive damaged and the supplier credits their price. The clerk writes the bill as 5(s + c) - 2c = 5s + c - 2c = 5s - c. Take s = 350 and c = 120. (a) Write the correct bill in simplest form. (b) Find the correct bill and the bill the clerk's expression gives. (c) By how much is the clerk's bill too low, in terms of c and in rupees? (d) Had three covers been damaged, write the correct bill in simplest form and find it.
questions.a: (a) 5(s + c) - 2c = 5s + 5c - 2c = 5s + 3c. (b) Correct: 5 × 350 + 3 × 120 = 1,750 + 360 = ₹2,110 (also 5 × 470 - 240 = 2,110). The clerk's 5s - c gives 1,750 - 120 = ₹1,630. (c) (5s + 3c) - (5s - c) = 4c = ₹480; the clerk multiplied only s by 5 and not c in the first step, so the bill is short by 4c. (d) 5(s + c) - 3c = 5s + 2c = 1,750 + 240 = ₹1,990.

questions.q: A shop's profit was (12a + 3b) rupees last month and (9a + 8b) rupees this month. For a = 10 and b = 4, what has happened to the profit from last month to this month?
questions.a: It has fallen by ₹10

questions.q: (a) Open the bracket and simplify 120 - (45 - m) + 15. (b) Find the value for m = 10 in two ways: from your simplest form and by working out the bracket first in the original.
s: Part (a): 90 + m, with the minus changing the sign of m

questions.q: A ribbon is (6a + 4b) cm long and a piece (2a - b) cm long is cut off it. (a) Write an expression for the ribbon left. (b) Simplify it. (c) Check with a = 5 and b = 2. (d) Check again with a = 3 and b = 4, and say whether two checks prove the simplification.
questions.a: (a) (6a + 4b) - (2a - b). (b) 6a + 4b - 2a + b = 4a + 5b. (c) (30 + 8) - (10 - 2) = 30 and 4 × 5 + 5 × 2 = 30. (d) (18 + 16) - (6 - 4) = 32 and 12 + 20 = 32. Two checks agree but only support the result; the algebra is what proves it for every a and b.
s: Part (b): 4a + 5b with the sign of b changed inside the bracket
Part (d): 32 both ways with the remark that checks alone do not prove

questions.q: True or False: -(x - 5) is the same as -x - 5, because the minus sign only has to be written before the first term. Test with x = 2 and give the reason or correction.
questions.a: False. For x = 2, -(2 - 5) = 3 but -2 - 5 = -7. The minus sign outside the bracket changes the sign of every term inside, so -(x - 5) = -x + 5.
s: States the verdict False, supported by the test values 3 and -7
Corrects it to -x + 5 because the minus changes the sign of both terms

questions.q:
Match each expression in Column I with its simplified form in Column II.
Column I: 1. 3(a + 2b) - 2a  2. 3(a - 2b) + 2a  3. 3a - 2(a + 2b)  4. 3a - 2(a - 2b)
Column II: A. a + 6b  B. 5a - 6b  C. a - 4b  D. a + 4b

Four students write the perimeter of a rectangle of length l and breadth b: A: l + b + l + b; B: 2l + 2b; C: 2(l + b); D: l + 2b. (a) Find the four values for l = 7 and b = 3. (b) Which one is not a correct perimeter formula? (c) Show that A and C both simplify to B. (d) By how much, in terms of l, does D fall short of the true perimeter? Check your answer with l = 7 and b = 3.
questions.a: (a) A 20, B 20, C 20, D 13. (b) D. (c) A: l + l + b + b = 2l + 2b; C: 2(l + b) = 2l + 2b. (d) (2l + 2b) - (l + 2b) = l, because D counts only one of the two lengths. Check: 20 - 13 = 7, which is l.
s: Part (c): shows A and C simplify to 2l + 2b
Part (d): shortfall l, because one length is left out

questions.q: Which expression is equal to 5(x + 2) - x for every x?

A shop bills n items by the formula 5(n + 3) + 2n rupees. A second clerk uses 7n + 15 and a third clerk uses 7n + 5. (a) Simplify the first formula and say whether it equals the second for every n. (b) Show that the third formula differs from the second for every n, and say by how much; check with n = 4.
questions.a: (a) 5n + 15 + 2n = 7n + 15, which is the second formula, so they are equal for every n. (b) (7n + 15) - (7n + 5) = 10, so the third clerk's bill is ₹10 less for every n. For n = 4 the bills are 43 and 33.
s: Part (a): 7n + 15, equal to the second formula
Part (b): the third differs by 10 for every n, with 43 and 33 at n = 4

questions.q: (a) Open the bracket in 9 - (a - 4) and simplify. (b) Aman says it equals 5 - a. Check this by putting a = 7 in the original, in your form and in Aman's.
questions.a: (a) 9 - a + 4 = 13 - a. (b) Original: 9 - (7 - 4) = 6. Mine: 13 - 7 = 6. Aman's: 5 - 7 = -2. So Aman is wrong; he changed only the sign of a and not of the 4.
s: Part (b): 6, 6 and -2, so Aman is wrong

questions.q:
Consider the following about equal expressions.
Statement 1: 4k - (k - 3) and 3k - 3 are equal for every value of k.
Statement 2: If 2x + 7 and 3x + 5 give the same value at x = 2, they give the same value at every x.
Statement 3: 3(k + 4) and 3k + 12 are equal for every value of k.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: 3 only

questions.q: Two mango vendors keep accounts. Pavan makes 18a - 5b in a week and Qadir makes 15a - 8b, where a is the money earned on each box sold and b the fuel cost of each delivery trip. (a) Write Pavan's amount minus Qadir's amount in simplest form. (b) Check your result for a = 4 and b = 1. (c) Check it again for a = 6 and b = 1. (d) Write Qadir's amount minus Pavan's amount in simplest form. (e) Who makes more when a and b are positive, and why?
questions.a: (a) (18a - 5b) - (15a - 8b) = 3a + 3b. (b) 67 - 52 = 15 and 3 × 4 + 3 × 1 = 15. (c) 103 - 82 = 21 and 3 × 6 + 3 × 1 = 21. (d) (15a - 8b) - (18a - 5b) = -3a - 3b, the opposite of part (a). (e) Pavan, since 3a + 3b is positive for positive a and b.
s: Part (e): Pavan, with the reason 3a + 3b is positive

questions.q: Is 7x - (3x + 2) equal to 4x + 2? Show a value of x where the two differ and write the correct simplest form of 7x - (3x + 2).
questions.a: No. For x = 1, 7 - 5 = 2 but 4 + 2 = 6. The correct form is 7x - 3x - 2 = 4x - 2.
s: Finds 2 for the first expression at x = 1
Finds 6 for 4x + 2 so they are not equal

questions.q: Two clerks write the hall-fee formula for p guests: Clerk A writes 3(p + 4) + 2p and Clerk B writes 5p + 12. Which statement is correct?
questions.a: They are equal, since A simplifies to 5p + 12

questions.q: A contractor lays a pavement in which row r has a certain number of tiles. Isha writes the number of tiles in row r as 3(r - 1) + 5. Jai writes it as 3r + 2. Kiran writes it as 2r + 3. The contractor needs to order tiles for row 40. (a) Find the three values for rows 1, 2 and 3. (b) Simplify Isha's expression and compare it with Jai's. (c) Say which of the three formulas can be trusted for every row, and why Kiran's first value does not settle the matter. (d) How many tiles would the contractor be short in row 40 if he used Kiran's formula instead of Jai's?
questions.a: (a) Isha: 5, 8, 11. Jai: 5, 8, 11. Kiran: 5, 7, 9. (b) 3r - 3 + 5 = 3r + 2, identical to Jai's. (c) Isha's and Jai's, which are equal for every r; Kiran's agrees only at row 1 and differs from row 2 onwards. (d) Jai's gives 3 × 40 + 2 = 122 and Kiran's gives 2 × 40 + 3 = 83, so he would be 39 tiles short.
s: Part (a): 5, 8, 11 for Isha and Jai and 5, 7, 9 for Kiran
Part (c): trusts Isha and Jai, Kiran agrees at row 1 only

questions.q: Vikram tests 2k + 6 and 2(k + 3) for k = 1, 2 and 3, finds equal values each time, and says they are equal for every k. Is his conclusion right? Is his method a proof?
questions.a: The values are 8, 10, 12 for both, and his conclusion is right: 2(k + 3) = 2k + 6 by the distributive property. But his method is not a proof, since three values do not cover every k; the distributive step is the proof.
s: Says testing values is not a proof

questions.q: (a) Simplify 3(a + 2) + a. (b) Say whether it is equal to 4a + 6 and whether it is equal to 4a + 2, giving the reason.
questions.a: (a) 3a + 6 + a = 4a + 6. (b) It is equal to 4a + 6, since the simplest forms are identical. It is not equal to 4a + 2, since for a = 0 they give 6 and 2.
s: Part (b): equal to 4a + 6 and not to 4a + 2, with a reason

questions.a: For example 2x + 10. At x = 4 both are 18. At x = 0, 3(x + 2) = 6 but 2x + 10 = 10, so they are not equal. (Any correct example is accepted.)

questions.q: Decide whether each pair is equal for every value of m, by simplifying one expression. (a) 3(m + 2) - m and 2m + 6. (b) 2(m + 4) - (m - 1) and m + 7. If a pair is not equal, give one value of m at which the two differ.
questions.a: (a) 3m + 6 - m = 2m + 6, so the pair is equal for every m. (b) 2m + 8 - m + 1 = m + 9, which is not m + 7; they differ for every m, for example at m = 0 where the values are 9 and 7.
s: Part (a): simplifies to 2m + 6 and says equal for every m
Part (b): simplifies to m + 9, says not equal, with a value such as m = 0 (9 and 7)

questions.q: For a school trip, the fee for n students is calculated by three spreadsheet formulas. Sheet A: 5(70n + 240). Sheet B: 350n + 1200. Sheet C: 450n + 200. The accountant checks them with n = 10 and says, 'All agree, so any sheet will do.' (a) Find the three values for n = 10. (b) Find the three values for n = 20 and for n = 0. (c) Simplify Sheet A and compare it with the others. (d) Which sheets are safe to use? If Sheet C were used for 32 students instead of B, what would be the difference in the total fee?
questions.a: (a) A, B and C all give ₹4,700. (b) n = 20: ₹8,200, ₹8,200, ₹9,200; n = 0: ₹1,200, ₹1,200, ₹200. (c) A = 350n + 1200, identical to B. (d) A and B are safe; C agrees only at n = 10. For 32 students B gives ₹12,400 and C gives ₹14,600, a difference of ₹2,200.
s: Part (b): values show C differs at n = 20 and n = 0
Part (c): A simplifies to 350n + 1200, equal to B
Part (d): A and B safe, C not, with ₹2,200 difference

questions.a: Lotus

questions.q: Meena says the nth term of 7, 10, 13, 16, ... is 3n + 7, because the pattern adds 3 and starts at 7. Test her formula and correct it if needed.
questions.a: For n = 1, 3n + 7 = 10, but the first term is 7, so she is wrong. The correct formula is 3n + 4, which gives 7, 10, 13, 16.

questions.q: Figure 1 of a dot pattern is hidden. Figures 2, 3 and 4 have 10, 14 and 18 dots and the rule continues. (a) How many dots does figure 1 have? (b) Write an expression for the dots in figure n and use it to find figure 25.
questions.a: (a) Each figure adds 4 dots, so figure 1 has 10 - 4 = 6 dots. (b) 4n + 2; figure 25 has 4 × 25 + 2 = 102 dots.

questions.q: Pattern 1 has 7 matchsticks in step 1 and adds 5 at every step. Pattern 2 has 12 matchsticks in step 1 and adds 3 at every step. (a) Write an expression for the matchsticks in step s of each pattern. (b) Which pattern has more in step 50, and by how many?
questions.a: (a) Pattern 1: 7 + 5(s - 1) = 5s + 2. Pattern 2: 12 + 3(s - 1) = 3s + 9. (b) Step 50: 252 and 159, so Pattern 1 has 93 more.

questions.q: A border repeats the four designs W, X, Y, Z in that order, and a lace below it repeats the six designs P, Q, R, S, T, U in that order. Both start together at position 1. Which pair of designs lies one above the other at position 30?
questions.a: X and U

questions.q: A number machine takes two inputs a and b and its rule has the form (a number) × a - (a number) × b. The inputs (4, 2), (5, 6) and (7, 1) produce 10, 9 and 20. Find its formula and use it for the inputs (6, 5).

questions.q: Pattern P has 6 matchsticks in step 1 and adds 2 at each step. Pattern Q has 3 matchsticks in step 1 and adds 3 at each step. (a) Write an expression in step y for each. (b) Find which pattern has more in step 2 and which has more in step 10.
questions.a: (a) P: 6 + 2(y - 1) = 2y + 4. Q: 3 + 3(y - 1) = 3y. (b) Step 2: P has 8 and Q has 6, so P has more. Step 10: P has 24 and Q has 30, so Q has more.
s: Part (b): P ahead at step 2 (8 against 6), Q ahead at step 10 (30 against 24)

questions.q: The numbers 1, 2, 3, ... are written row by row in an endless grid of 4 columns. Column 3 holds 3, 7, 11, ... that is, 4n - 1. Show that 150 cannot be in column 3.
questions.a: In column 3 the numbers near 150 are 4 × 37 - 1 = 147 and 4 × 38 - 1 = 151. They jump from 147 to 151, so 150 is not in column 3 (it leaves remainder 2 on dividing by 4, so it is in column 2).
s: Concludes 150 is skipped and is not in column 3

questions.q: A row of squares is made from matchsticks. One square needs 4 sticks and each extra square, joined to the last, needs 3 more sticks. (a) List the sticks for 1 to 5 squares. (b) Write an expression for n squares that starts with 4. (c) Simplify it to a shorter form. (d) Find the sticks for 40 squares. (e) Find the sticks for 33 squares and for 34 squares, and say from which number of squares the count first goes above 100.
s: Part (e): 100 for 33 squares, 103 for 34, so above 100 from 34 squares

questions.q: A saree border repeats five designs A, B, C, D, E in that order. (a) Use the remainder on dividing by 5 to find the design at position 138. (b) How many times does design D appear in the first 138 positions?
questions.a: (a) 138 = 5 × 27 + 3, remainder 3, so design C. (b) 27 complete cycles of five each hold one D, and the 3 places left over (A, B, C) hold none, so D appears 27 times.
s: Part (b): 27 complete cycles, none in the leftover A, B, C, so 27

questions.q: For a family function, square tables are hired for ₹150 each. One table alone seats 4 guests. If tables are joined end to end in one long row, 2 tables seat 6, 3 tables seat 8, and the pattern continues. (a) How many guests do 5 joined tables seat? (b) Write an expression for the guests seated by n tables joined in one row. (c) The helper says the expression is 2n + 4, 'because each table adds 2 and the first table has 4'. Test his formula with n = 1 and n = 3 and say what he did wrong. (d) Find the number of joined tables needed for 30 guests and for 31 guests, and the hire cost in each case.
questions.a: (a) 12. (b) 4 + 2(n - 1) = 2n + 2. (c) His formula gives 6 for n = 1 (the real number is 4) and 10 for n = 3 (the real number is 8). He added 2 for the first table as well, but the first table is already counted in the 4; only the n - 1 tables after it add 2 each. (d) For 30 guests, 14 tables seat exactly 2 × 14 + 2 = 30, costing 14 × 150 = ₹2,100. For 31 guests, 14 tables are one seat short, so 15 tables are needed (they seat 32), costing 15 × 150 = ₹2,250.
s: Part (c): 6 against 4 and 10 against 8, with the reason that the first table adds no extra 2

questions.q: Write the first four terms of the pattern whose nth term is 6n - 1. Then make up a real-life situation that this pattern could describe.
questions.a: 5, 11, 17, 23. For example, a shop sells packets of 6 pencils and each customer gets 1 pencil less than a full packet; n packets, less one pencil, give 6n - 1 pencils. (Any consistent situation is accepted.)
s: Explains the 6 per step and the 1 taken away

questions.q: A weaver makes a saree border of exactly 250 motifs that repeat four motifs in this order: peacock, lotus, fish, elephant. An elephant costs ₹70 to weave and every other motif costs ₹40. (a) Write the positions of the elephants, and find which motif is at position 250. (b) How many elephants are in the border? (c) The assistant says there are 63 lotuses and also 63 elephants, 'because 250 divided by 4 is more than 62'. Check his claim by counting the lotuses and the elephants. (d) Find the weaving cost of the whole border.
questions.a: (a) Elephants are at positions 4n. 250 = 4 × 62 + 2, remainder 2, so position 250 is a lotus. (b) The last elephant is at 4 × 62 = 248, since 4 × 63 = 252 is beyond 250; there are 62 elephants. (c) Lotuses are at positions 4n - 2, and 4 × 63 - 2 = 250, so there are 63 lotuses; but there are only 62 elephants. His claim is right for the lotuses and wrong for the elephants. (d) 62 × 70 = 4,340 for elephants and 188 × 40 = 7,520 for the other motifs, a total of ₹11,860.
s: Part (a): elephants at 4n, and a lotus at position 250 from remainder 2
Part (c): 63 lotuses but 62 elephants, so the claim is half right
